headline: Obaidul Kader and 6 others sentenced to death for crimes against humanity
summary: International Crimes Tribunal-2 has ordered the execution of seven top leaders from the Awami League, Jubo League, and Chhatra League for their roles in the July mass uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 sentenced seven top leaders, including Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Kader, to death for crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising.
caption:

topic: dengue deaths rise, new hospital admissions surge
headline_marked: 7 dead, 1,593 hospitalized in [[last 24 hours due to dengue]]
headline: 7 dead, 1,593 hospitalized in last 24 hours due to dengue
summary: The health department reports a surge in cases, with September's first half showing an alarming increase in both infections and deaths compared to August.
details: Seven people, including four women and three men, died from dengue in the last 24 hours, according to the Health Emergency Operation Center and Control Room of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
During the same period, 1,593 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the country, with the highest number of admissions in the Dhaka division (excluding city corporations).
Data shows that the 21-25 age group was the most affected among new admissions, with 253 people in this age bracket hospitalized.
Since January 1, this year, a total of 55,163 people have been infected with dengue, resulting in 164 deaths. Of the deceased, 52.4% were women and 47.6% were men.
The situation has become more concerning in September. While 20,536 people were infected and 43 died in August, the first 15 days of September have already seen 19,317 infections and 67 deaths.
Currently, 4,058 dengue patients remain hospitalized across various facilities in Bangladesh.
Among the city corporations, Dhaka South City Corporation has recorded the highest number of deaths, with 51 people losing their lives so far this year.
caption:
7 deaths and nearly 1,600 hospitalizations in just 24 hours. Dengue cases are surging at an alarming rate.

Seven people, including four women and three men, died from dengue in the last 24 hours, according to the Health Emergency Operation Center and Control Room of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

During the same period, 1,593 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the country, with the highest number of admissions in the Dhaka division (excluding city corporations).

Data shows that the 21-25 age group was the most affected among new admissions, with 253 people in this age bracket hospitalized.

Since January 1, this year, a total of 55,163 people have been infected with dengue, resulting in 164 deaths. Of the deceased, 52.4% were women and 47.6% were men.

The situation has become more concerning in September. While 20,536 people were infected and 43 died in August, the first 15 days of September have already seen 19,317 infections and 67 deaths.

Currently, 4,058 dengue patients remain hospitalized across various facilities in Bangladesh.

Among the city corporations, Dhaka South City Corporation has recorded the highest number of deaths, with 51 people losing their lives so far this year.
